title: 1494年的未完比赛：帕乔利为何难以定义公平
scope: Only chapter 02; global book evidence_verified remains false.

claims.statement: Pacioli Summa was printed at Venice in 1494
The original Pacioli ballgame example was target 60, ten points per score, interrupted at 50:20, total 10 ducats
claims.caution: Original printed page images not independently inspected

claims.statement: Pacioli's division rule used already obtained scores 50:20=5:2; 10 ducats yielded 50/7 and 20/7
Tartaglia 1556 used different example figures (50:30, 22 ducats in retelling), rebutted 10:0 case, and offered different rule
claims.caution: Do not conflate with original 1494 50:20 and 10 total

claims.statement: Cardano criticized Pacioli in 1539 work, and issue is attested by earlier manuscript traditions
claims.caution: Dates and interpretations of earliest manuscripts need primary archive check

claims.statement: Pascal and Fermat exchanged correspondence on points problem in 1654
Under newly imposed independent fair round assumptions at 50:20 to 60, trailing party wins only by winning next four: 1/16; leading party 15/16
assumptions: Each next 10-point round equally likely 1/2 for either side
claims.caution: Not a historical claim or a real-world match probability

sources.title: Pulskamp, The Problem of Points history
